title: E-commerce Customer Analysis
findings: 1,607 of 3,370 eligible customers made a second observed invoice within 90 calendar days.
Average identified invoice value was £480.87, excluding cancellation and nonpositive lines.
132,220 otherwise qualifying lines lack customer IDs and are excluded from customer analysis.
action: Test a post-purchase message using a randomized holdout and track 90-day repeat purchases and contribution margin among eligible customers.

chart.title: 90-day repeat rate by first observed month

problem: How often did identifiable customers place another invoice within a comparable 90-day observation period?
grain: The source is invoice-line data from a UK online retailer, 1 Dec 2010 to 9 Dec 2011. This analysis groups positive lines into customer/invoice purchases.
definitions: An order is a distinct CustomerID and InvoiceNo combination in the cleaned data.
Average invoice value = total included line value for identified customers ÷ distinct identified customer/invoice orders.
First observed purchase is the earliest included invoice in this dataset, not necessarily a lifetime first purchase.
90-day repeat rate = eligible customers with at least two distinct invoices by 90 calendar days after first observed purchase ÷ eligible customers.
Eligible means first observed purchase is at least 90 calendar days before the final observed date. Same-day distinct invoices count.
caveats: Only identified transactions are included. The dataset has no pre-window customer history, and the source is a gift retailer with wholesale customers. Cancellation and negative lines are excluded without matching to original invoices, so values are not net of returns. Observed repeat is not lifetime retention; customers may place orders outside the data window.
nextsteps: Reconcile returns and join earlier order history to distinguish new customers from first observed customers.
Compare mature cohorts over equal follow-up windows and segment wholesale accounts separately.
Randomize a retention intervention and measure incremental gross profit after message costs.
quality: 541,909 source lines; 9,288 cancellation-prefixed lines; 11,805 nonpositive quantity or price lines; 11,805 excluded by either rule; 135,080 source lines lack customer ID. These categories overlap. 5,268 exact duplicate-looking rows are retained because they may represent distinct invoice lines. Among otherwise qualifying lines, 132,220 lack customer ID and are excluded from customer metrics.
citation: Chen, D. (2015), Online Retail, UCI Machine Learning Repository, https://doi.org/10.24432/C5BW33 (CC BY 4.0).
